item.title: RBA set for back-to-back hike after hot CPI, says Natixis’ Garcia Herrero
item.description:
A back-to-back hike would extend the Australian dollar’s rate advantage and keep front-end yields elevated, while any hint that November is the last move could trigger a pullback in both. Fuel is the key transmission channel, so oil prices remain central to the outlook: further crude gains would deepen the pass-through into services and strengthen calls for more tightening. Australian equities, particularly rate-sensitive sectors such as property and consumer discretionary, face added pressure if markets begin to price a longer hiking path.

---

Earlier:

  • ING lifts AUD/USD target to 0.71 as it backs a 25bp RBA hike next week

---

Fuel is no longer just a petrol-station problem for Australia’s inflation, and Natixis expects the RBA to respond again next week.

Summary:

  • September CPI rose about 0.8% m/m and 4.3% y/y, above forecasts of 0.7% and 4.2%
  • Energy added about 0.3 points to the monthly rise, while travel contributed around 0.43 points, its most since December 2025
  • Garcia Herrero sees the energy shock passing through to the broader basket
  • The Q3 trimmed mean edged up to about 3.7%, diverging from the RBA’s August forecast of a peak in Q2
  • Hauser and Bullock comments reinforce the RBA’s low tolerance for persistent inflation
  • Natixis expects a back-to-back hike on 3 November, with later decisions highly data dependent

Australia’s September inflation data delivered a sharp upside surprise that is likely to push the Reserve Bank of Australia into a back-to-back rate hike at its meeting on Tuesday, 3 November. That is the view of Alicia Garcia Herrero, chief economist for Asia Pacific at Natixis and one of the more closely followed analysts of the RBA.

Headline consumer prices rose about 0.8% in September from August and around 4.3% from a year earlier, both ahead of consensus forecasts of 0.7% and 4.2%. Garcia Herrero said the print surprised the market as well as the central bank.

The detail is what concerns her most. Energy added roughly a third of a percentage point to the monthly increase, but travel was the single largest driver, contributing around 0.43 percentage points, its biggest contribution since December 2025. Travel prices are closely tied to fuel costs, so Garcia Herrero said the data suggest the energy shock has begun to filter through to the wider basket of goods and services. She described this as a warning sign for policymakers.

Underlying inflation is also moving away from the path the RBA expected. The trimmed mean, the central bank’s preferred core measure, rose to about 3.7% year on year in the third quarter, edging up from the second quarter. In August, the RBA had projected that the trimmed mean would peak in the second quarter and ease back towards 3.3% by the end of 2026. The latest reading widens the gap between that forecast and the actual inflation path.

Garcia Herrero linked the data to recent comments from RBA officials. Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser recently described the inflation outlook as having deteriorated materially. Governor Michele Bullock told a parliamentary hearing this week that the central bank will not tolerate inflation remaining persistently high. Against that backdrop, Garcia Herrero expects the RBA to favour another hike next week.

Beyond November, she expects policy to become more finely balanced. The RBA is likely to keep a hawkish tone while inflation remains elevated. However, signs of an easing labour market and slowing household spending under higher interest rates mean subsequent decisions are likely to be highly data dependent. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: ING lifts AUD/USD target to 0.71 as it backs a 25bp RBA hike next week
item.description:
Front-end Australian yields look most exposed to next week’s decision, with roughly 5bp of hike pricing still to close if the RBA moves. A hold would likely hit the Australian dollar hard, given how much of its October strength rests on rate expectations. Oil is a key driver: further gains in crude would add to fuel-led inflation and reinforce the tightening bias, while a sustained pullback could ease pressure on the RBA. The Fed’s stance remains the main external constraint on AUD/USD.

---

Earlier:

  • RBA set for fifth 2026 hike to 4.85% as banks flag risk of another move in February

---

ING likes the Aussie’s yield and expects the RBA to add to it next week, but sees the Fed standing between AUD/USD and 0.72.

Summary:

  • ING raised its short-term AUD/USD target to 0.71, but doesn’t expect a return to 0.72 this quarter
  • It says the Australian dollar offers the best volatility-adjusted short-term carry in G10
  • ING expects a 25bp RBA hike on 3 November, taking the cash rate to 4.85%, against about 20bp priced
  • Headline CPI hit 4.3% y/y in September, driven almost entirely by fuel-related transport costs
  • Goods and services inflation are both above 4%, and core inflation accelerated
  • A hawkish Fed is expected to keep supporting the US dollar, limiting AUD gains

ING has raised its short-term forecast for the Australian dollar to 0.71 against the US dollar, citing the currency’s strong October and its attractive yield advantage. The bank does not expect AUD/USD to climb back to 0.72 this quarter, however, as a hawkish Federal Reserve keeps supporting the greenback.

The upgrade rests on ING’s view that the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise its cash rate by 25 basis points at its 3 November meeting, rather than waiting until December. That would lift the cash rate to 4.85%. The bank had previously pencilled in a hike at some point in the fourth quarter, and now sees the latest inflation data as strong enough to bring the move forward. Markets are pricing around 20 basis points of tightening for next week, slightly short of a full hike.

ING said AUD/USD is driven mainly by short-term interest rate differentials. It added that the Australian dollar currently offers the best short-term carry in the G10 once volatility is taken into account. Carry refers to the return investors earn from holding a higher-yielding currency, and a further RBA hike would widen that advantage.

The inflation backdrop supports the case. Headline consumer prices rose 4.3% from a year earlier in September, with inflation picking up by about 90 basis points between July and September, based on the latest monthly figures and the third-quarter report. Almost all of that increase came from transport costs, largely reflecting higher fuel prices. ING noted that goods and services inflation are both now running above 4%, a sign that energy costs are spreading more widely through the economy. Core inflation also accelerated on both annual and quarterly measures. The trimmed mean rose to 3.7%, above forecasts and well above the RBA’s target band.

ING concluded that underlying inflation is not on a sustained downward path, weakening any argument for a pause. At its last meeting, the RBA raised rates unanimously and signalled it was prepared to accept some softening in the labour market to bring inflation back to target.

The main limit on further Australian dollar gains lies outside Australia. With the Fed also leaning hawkish, ING expects the US dollar to remain supported, capping the upside for AUD/USD in the near term even if the RBA delivers next week.

item.title: ECB to hike once more in December as tighter conditions may not suffice: Deutsche Bank
item.description:
A December “last hike” view mainly affects the euro front end, with Euribor, €STR futures and one- to two-year government bond yields most exposed to shifts in pricing. Capping expectations could reduce volatility further out the curve, while short-dated contracts stay sensitive to each inflation print. Energy is the swing factor: further gains in oil and gas prices would strengthen the case for tightening and could support the euro. Leadership uncertainty adds a policy risk premium into 2027, which could weigh on the single currency if succession becomes politically contested.

---

Earlier:

  • investingLive Americas market news wrap: ECB holds, sources report says December hike

---

Deutsche Bank thinks the ECB has one more hike in it, and that the coming change of personnel matters less than the price of energy.

Summary:

  • Deutsche Bank expects one more ECB rate hike in December, likely the last of the cycle
  • Its view is that hikes so far and tighter financial conditions may not be enough if energy prices keep rising
  • The ECB held all three key rates on Thursday, with the deposit rate at 2.5%, as Deutsche Bank expected
  • Lagarde will step down in February, Schnabel leaves in January and Lane’s term ends in May
  • Deutsche Bank says the leadership changes make the path harder to predict but do not automatically alter it
  • Knot and Hernández de Cos are among the early contenders to succeed Lagarde

Deutsche Bank expects the European Central Bank to raise interest rates one more time in December. It argues that the tightening already delivered may not be enough to contain inflation if energy prices keep rising.

The call follows Thursday’s ECB meeting, at which policymakers held all three key interest rates steady, leaving the deposit rate at 2.5%. Deutsche Bank had expected the pause, describing it as a measured response to the energy price shock. The euro and euro zone bond yields fell after the decision.

Mark Wall, chief European economist at Deutsche Bank Research, said the rate increases delivered so far are unlikely to be sufficient on their own if energy costs continue to feed through to consumer prices, even together with the tightening in financial conditions since September. The bank therefore still sees a final hike in December, a move it regards as the likely end of the current tightening cycle.

Wall also acknowledged that forecasting the ECB’s path has become more difficult, in part because of a wave of leadership changes at the central bank. President Christine Lagarde will step down in February, roughly nine months before her eight-year term was due to end in October 2027. She is only the second ECB president to leave early. Executive board member Isabel Schnabel is also departing a year early, in January, to take up a senior role at the International Monetary Fund. Chief economist Philip Lane’s term expires in May.

The race to succeed Lagarde is already under way. The Dutch government is backing former Dutch central bank governor Klaas Knot, while Spain supports Pablo Hernández de Cos, general manager of the Bank for International Settlements and a former Bank of Spain governor.

Wall questioned whether the leadership changes would alter decision-making. He argued that the ECB as an institution is bigger than any single president and that a new head does not automatically mean a different rate path.

If Deutsche Bank is right, the December move would set a ceiling on near-term rate expectations and shift the debate from how high rates go to how long they stay there. The new leadership’s tone in 2027 will then become the key question for markets.

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Intel earnings call: 18A progress and data centre growth offset by PC slump and cash burn
item.description:
The call is unlikely to reverse the after-hours drop on its own, since the near-term numbers carry more weight than roadmap milestones when guidance is this weak. The bigger read-across is to the PC supply chain. Management’s account of aggressive OEM inventory cuts points to pressure on PC makers, memory suppliers and Asian component manufacturers in coming quarters. The substrate shortage is a supply-side constraint that may benefit packaging material suppliers. The server growth estimate, though a company projection, adds to the broader case for data centre spending that has supported chip stocks this year.

---

Earlier:

  • Earnings bloodbath: Intel crashes over 22%, Amazon over 12%. What's coming next?
  • Intel shares tumble around 15%. The narrative is --> weak Q4 guidance overshadows Q3 profit beat
  • Intel beats Q3 profit forecasts, but weak Q4 guidance and PC outlook weigh. Share price drops.

---

Intel’s call offered a credible roadmap for the long run and a bruising list of problems for the next few quarters, and the market is paid to price the latter first.

Summary:

  • Supportive: The first 18A server chip is shipping for revenue, and the first 18A-P server product is on track to ramp in 2027
  • Supportive: Client chips are progressing, with Nova Lake ahead of schedule and Wildcat Lake demand ahead of supply; 18A-P and 14A are on track
  • Supportive: Intel is engaged with a couple of strategic external foundry customers, 18A costs are down about 40% since Q1, and data centre revenue is seen up mid-teens in Q4
  • Supportive: Intel estimates the server CPU market could grow fivefold to more than $200 billion over five years
  • Caution: The PC correction has accelerated; client revenue is seen down more than 20% in Q4 and 2026 PC units down about 12%
  • Caution: A substrate shortage is limiting output, capex is rising strongly into 2027, and no positive cash flow is expected this year

Intel’s post-earnings conference call gave investors material to support both sides of the argument after the shares fell around 20% in after-hours trading on weak fourth-quarter guidance. Management pointed to steady progress on its manufacturing roadmap and strong data centre demand. It also described a PC slump that has worsened quickly and warned that cash flow will remain under pressure.

On the supportive side, the chief executive said Clearwater Forest, the company’s first server processor built on its Intel 18A manufacturing process, is now shipping for revenue. Diamond Rapids, its first server product on the more advanced 18A-P process, is sampling and on track to ramp in 2027. On the PC side, Panther Lake has been ramped on 18A and demand for Wildcat Lake is running ahead of supply. Nova Lake, the first client chip on 18A-P, is tracking ahead of schedule, with design wins expected to be double those of Panther Lake at launch. The 18A-P process remains on course for launch across Intel’s own products by year end, and the next-generation 14A process is also on track.

Intel said it is engaged with a couple of external customers it described as highly strategic for 18A-P, a potentially important step for its foundry ambitions. The company also estimates the market for server processors could grow as much as fivefold over five years, from about $40 billion to more than $200 billion. The finance chief said 18A costs have fallen roughly 40% since the first quarter. Data centre and AI revenue should grow by a mid-teens percentage from the third quarter to the fourth.

The case for caution centres on PCs and cash. The chief executive said the PC correction has accelerated over the past two months, as computer makers aggressively cut inventory to match softer end demand. Intel expects client computing revenue to fall by more than 20% from the third quarter. It now sees 2026 PC unit sales declining about 12%, with second-half units down more than 20%. An industry-wide shortage of advanced substrates used in its EMIB chip packaging is also limiting its ability to scale output.

Spending is heavy and rising. Gross capital expenditure remains on track for $20 billion this year, and the company expects it to rise strongly in 2027, with equipment spending set to climb further next quarter. The finance chief does not expect positive cash flow this year and also indicated that a factor related to Israel would likely weigh mainly on fourth-quarter margins. Intel expects payments to minority partners in its joint ventures, known as non-controlling interest, of about $250 million in the fourth quarter. It sees around $1.1 billion in each of 2027 and 2028, reducing the profit that flows to shareholders.

The call leaves a clear split for investors. The technology roadmap and data centre outlook support the longer-term turnaround story. The PC downturn, supply constraints and rising spending point to a difficult few quarters before those gains show up in earnings and cash flow 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Binance appears hacked, CZ says, as Tether and Circle freeze $1.79B in stablecoins
item.description:
CZ’s comments take away part of the uncertainty but not the core risk. He has confirmed a likely hack, while the person who can commit Binance’s money to cover losses has said nothing yet. The stablecoin freezes shrink the possible loss, but the ether moved out of Binance has no such protection. BNB is the clearest gauge of how worried traders are, and it is likely to stay under pressure until Binance commits to covering losses. Bitcoin and ether are falling with the rest of the market rather than for a reason specific to them, so they could recover faster if Binance gives clear reassurance.

---

Earlier:

  • Tether freezes $971M USDT amid suspected Binance hack as crypto sells off

---

CZ calls it a hack and says user funds are safe, Tether and Circle have locked up $1.79 billion, and Binance has yet to say how much it lost.

Summary:

  • Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) said the exchange appears to have been hacked and that user funds are safe.
  • Tether froze about $971 million in USDT and Circle froze about $823 million in USDC, around $1.79 billion in total.
  • CZ said he no longer runs Binance but, as a shareholder, expects all user funds to be fully covered. This is not a formal pledge from Binance.
  • Binance said it is investigating a potential security issue. It has not confirmed the losses or how the transfers happened.
  • More than $2 billion moved from Binance wallets to a new address, including about 167,000 ETH, which can’t be frozen.
  • BNB fell about 6% to near $710. Bitcoin dropped about 2% and ether about 3%.

Binance appears to have been hacked, co-founder Changpeng Zhao said on Thursday, 29 October, as stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze about $1.79 billion in tokens linked to more than $2 billion that left the exchange’s wallets. Zhao, widely known as CZ, said user funds are safe.

In a post on X, Zhao said the activity does look like a hack on Binance. He thanked Tether for freezing roughly $971 million in USDT and Circle for freezing about $823 million in USDC. He added that he no longer manages Binance but, as a shareholder, expects all user funds to be fully covered. Zhao stepped down as chief executive in 2023, so his comments are not a formal reimbursement pledge from the exchange.

Binance itself has gone less far. In a statement on X, it said its teams were aware of reports of a potential security issue and were actively investigating, Cryptowisser reported. It did not confirm a breach, the amount involved or how the transfers happened.

Crypto prices fell as the news spread. Binance’s own BNB token, which is used for trading-fee discounts on the exchange and to pay fees on its affiliated BNB Chain blockchain, was hit hardest among the large caps. It was down almost 6% near $710, according to Cryptowisser price data. Bitcoin was down about 2% near $79,400, and ether lost about 3% to around $2,280. CoinGlass data cited by Crypto News Flash showed about $620 million in liquidations in one hour as the reports broke, roughly 97% of them long positions.

On-chain data first circulated by market news account Walter Bloomberg showed about $2.77 billion leaving Binance wallets across five blockchains. Coindoo, checking Etherscan, found two large Ethereum transfers to the same newly created address. One came from a wallet labelled Binance 14 and included about 167,000 ETH and roughly 1.6 billion USDT. The second was 780 million USDC from a Binance hot wallet. On-chain investigators claim the receiving address was funded through Tornado Cash, a mixing service that hides where funds come from, though that remains unverified.

The freezes matter because they put a large share of the stolen stablecoins out of the attacker’s reach. Tether and Circle can block addresses through controls built into their token contracts, which stops frozen tokens from moving. The ether in the flow, worth roughly $380 million at current prices, has no such safeguard, and frozen funds are not automatically returned to their owners.

The key questions now are how much Binance actually lost once the freezes are counted, whether withdrawals continue normally, and whether Binance itself commits to covering any losses. If confirmed at anything near the reported scale, the incident would rank among the largest crypto thefts on record. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Tether freezes $971M USDT amid suspected Binance hack as crypto sells off
item.description:
BNB took the heaviest hit among large caps, which shows traders pricing exchange-specific risk rather than a broad macro shock. Long positions took the damage, so the drop looks driven by forced selling more than by fresh shorts, and that can reverse quickly if the scare fades. The key swing factor is Binance’s silence. Confirmation of a breach would likely deepen pressure on BNB and on confidence in exchange custody. Proof that the funds are still under Binance’s control would remove the catalyst. Until one or the other happens, expect thin liquidity and headline-driven price swings.

---

A $971 million Tether freeze turns a murky $2.77 billion Binance outflow into the market’s biggest worry, and Binance’s silence is keeping crypto on edge.

Summary:

  • Tether has frozen $971 million in USDT amid a suspected Binance hack, per newswire headlines.
  • On-chain data showed about $2.77 billion leaving Binance wallets across five blockchains late on 29 October. Binance has not commented, and a breach is unconfirmed.
  • Etherscan shows two large transfers to one new address. One included about 167,000 ETH and 1.6 billion USDT, and the other was 780 million USDC.
  • BNB fell almost 7% to near $700. Bitcoin slipped to about $78,900 and ether lost 4%.
  • Liquidations hit about $620 million in one hour, roughly 97% of them longs.
  • Claims that the receiving address was funded through Tornado Cash are unverified. No security firm has tied the moves to theft.

Tether has frozen $971 million in USDT amid a suspected hack at Binance, according to newswire headlines, after on-chain data showed about $2.77 billion leaving the exchange’s wallets across five blockchains late on Thursday, 29 October. Binance has yet to issue an update, and a breach has not been confirmed.

Crypto sold off as the reports spread. As of about 21:00 GMT, bitcoin was trading near $78,900, down roughly 2.6% over 24 hours, while ether fell about 4% to around $2,257. Binance’s own BNB token was hit hardest among the large caps, sliding almost 7% to near $700, including a drop of about 6% in a single hour, Crypto News Flash reported. XRP and Solana each lost more than 5%.

The move caught leveraged traders leaning the wrong way. CoinGlass data cited by Crypto News Flash showed about $620 million in liquidations in one hour, roughly 97% of them long positions, taking the 24-hour total to about $951 million.

The outflow figure was first circulated on X by market news account Walter Bloomberg, which described it as a suspected hack that had not been confirmed. Coindoo, checking Etherscan, found two large Ethereum transfers to the same newly created address around 20:24 and 20:41 GMT. One came from a wallet labelled Binance 14 and included about 167,000 ETH and roughly 1.6 billion USDT. The second was 780 million USDC from a Binance hot wallet. Some on-chain investigators have claimed the receiving address was funded through Tornado Cash, a crypto mixing service that obscures where funds come from. That link has not been independently verified, and no blockchain security firm has publicly tied the transfers to theft.

The Tether freeze matters because it would be one of the largest the stablecoin issuer has carried out, nearly three times the $344 million it froze with US authorities in April. Tether can blacklist addresses through a function built into the USDT smart contract, which blocks the frozen tokens from moving. That only covers USDT, though. Any ether, USDC or other tokens in the flow sit outside Tether’s reach, and a freeze does not automatically return funds to their owners.

There is a credible innocent explanation, which is why caution is warranted. Large exchanges regularly shuffle funds between hot and cold wallets. In February, Binance disputed viral claims of $10 billion to $17 billion in withdrawals, saying third-party data contained discrepancies. A Tether freeze of this size, however, is harder to square with a routine reshuffle.

Traders will now look for a Binance statement on whether customer funds are affected and whether withdrawals are running normally. They will also want attribution from security firms on who controls the receiving address. If a breach is confirmed, it would rank among the largest crypto thefts on record and could keep pressure on BNB and the wider market. If Binance shows the funds remain in its control, the selloff could unwind as quickly as it arrived. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Earnings bloodbath: Intel crashes over 22%, Amazon over 12%. What's coming next?
item.description:
Amazon and Intel stocks tumble after earnings. Strong AI growth wasn't enough

Amazon's cloud sales jumped 39% and Intel's data-center revenue rose 78%, yet both stocks sold off sharply. Investors are questioning the cost and sustainability of growth. Here are the important price levels to watch as Friday's trading approaches.

Amazon (AMZN) and Intel (INTC) shares fell sharply after their October 29 earnings releases, despite impressive growth in their cloud and data-center businesses. Amazon's heavy AI investment is consuming free cash flow, while Intel's weak outlook raises questions about its recovery. For traders, the next test is whether the initial after-hours selling attracts lasting buying interest.

As of 4:50 p.m. New York time on Thursday, October 29, 2026, before the scheduled 5 p.m. earnings calls:

  • Amazon: Approximately $228.62, down 6.4% from its final pre-release five-minute reference near $244.23.

  • Intel: Approximately $76.83, down 16.6% from its corresponding reference near $92.08.

  • Nasdaq futures: Down approximately 1.23% over the comparable initial reaction window.

These are after-hours observations, not regular-session closing prices or live quotations.

Amazon: AWS is booming, but investors want to see the cash

Amazon delivered a quarter with several genuinely impressive numbers.

According to its official Q3 earnings announcement, revenue increased 12% to approximately $201.94 billion, narrowly missing Wall Street expectations near $202.2 billion.

Amazon Web Services was a standout. Revenue reached approximately $46 billion, up 39.3% from a year earlier, marking its fastest growth in nearly five years.

Operating income rose to $28.1 billion, producing a record operating margin of 13.9%.

Those figures do not describe a business struggling to generate growth or operating profits.

So why did the shares fall?

The answer appears to lie in what that growth costs, how much cash it consumes and whether investors believe future returns will justify today's investment.

Amazon reported negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion over the trailing 12 months, compared with positive free cash flow of $14.8 billion in the comparable period a year earlier.

That is a deterioration of $57.2 billion.

Importantly, this does not mean Amazon's operations stopped generating cash. Trailing 12-month operating cash flow actually increased 29% to $168.3 billion. The difference is largely associated with the enormous investment required to build infrastructure, especially for AI.

Management maintained its outlook for approximately $220 billion in 2026 cash capital expenditures.

Meanwhile, fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $240 billion to $247 billion puts the midpoint at $243.5 billion, modestly below analyst expectations near $244.5 billion.

Reported third-quarter earnings of $1.89 per share also missed estimates around $1.97. However, the year-earlier EPS comparison was inflated by $9.5 billion in pretax gains from Amazon's Anthropic investments. It would therefore be misleading to interpret the year-over-year headline EPS movement as evidence of comparable weakness in its underlying operations.

The emerging question is not whether Amazon can grow its AI business. The latest results demonstrate substantial demand.

The more difficult question is how much shareholders ultimately receive from that growth after funding the infrastructure needed to deliver it.

That is a different standard from simply reporting rapid cloud revenue expansion.

Amazon stock: The first rebound has already recovered substantial ground

The initial price reaction was severe.

Amazon fell from its pre-release five-minute reference near $244.23 to an after-hours low around $214.01, a decline of approximately 12.4%.

Buyers then returned, lifting the shares substantially off that low.

By the 4:50 p.m. ET data cutoff, Amazon was trading around $228.62, still approximately 6.4% below the reference.

That recovery is worth watching, but it is not yet sufficient evidence that the selling has ended.

Amazon share-price levels to watch

$224.90-$229.10: The first stabilization test

This is the immediate area where traders can assess whether the rebound is developing a foundation.

Holding this region on subsequent pullbacks would improve the short-term recovery case. Repeated failures to defend it would leave the stock vulnerable to renewed pressure.

$232.30-$234.90: The first meaningful recovery hurdle

If buyers push beyond the initial stabilization zone, this is the next area where the strength of the rebound can be evaluated.

A brief price spike into the region is less meaningful than a sustained move above it, followed by evidence that buyers can defend the reclaimed prices.

$239.70-$244.25: The higher recovery region

This area extends toward Amazon's pre-earnings price reference.

Reaching it would represent a much more substantial recovery from the earnings shock. It would not, by itself, resolve concerns about AI spending or free cash flow.

$219.70, followed by $213-$214: Downside areas

A renewed breakdown would put the first lower observation level near $219.70 into focus.

Below that, the market would be approaching the initial earnings low. Whether buyers defend that low, or sellers force prices through it, could help determine the next phase.

Intel: Strong data-center growth meets a much weaker forecast

Intel's selloff was considerably more severe, despite an earnings report that contained encouraging signs of operational improvement.

Its official third-quarter results showed revenue increasing 21% to approximately $16.5 billion.

Non-GAAP earnings reached $0.52 per share, ahead of analyst expectations near $0.40. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.60.

Intel's Data Center and AI business increased revenue 78% to $7.3 billion.

GAAP gross margin also improved to 43%, compared with 38.2% a year earlier.

Yet the market reaction demonstrates the danger of looking at the quarter in isolation.

Intel expects fourth-quarter revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion. The midpoint of $15.5 billion is approximately 9.2% below the $17.07 billion consensus cited by Reuters.

The company also forecasts fourth-quarter non-GAAP EPS of $0.25, substantially below expectations around $0.43.

That is a significant gap in forward expectations, especially for a company whose stock had already experienced a powerful rally during 2026.

The personal-computer business presents another challenge. Revenue from Intel's Client Computing and Physical AI group declined 5% to $8.1 billion, and management expects weakness in the PC market to persist at least through the first half of 2027.

There is also an important manufacturing issue.

Reuters reports that an October disruption at Intel's Kiryat Gat production facility in Israel is expected to reduce revenue by approximately $300 million in the fourth quarter and a similar amount in the first quarter of 2027.

That adds a specific near-term supply constraint to the broader demand and execution challenges.

For Intel shareholders, the positive development is that data-center demand and operating performance have improved significantly.

The negative is that those improvements are not currently sufficient to prevent a sharp downgrade in the near-term outlook.

Intel stock: A rebound doesn't necessarily mean the bottom is in

Intel's immediate after-hours response was dramatic.

From approximately $92.08 before the announcement, the shares fell to $71.20, a decline of roughly 22.7%.

A rebound subsequently lifted the stock as high as $79.16.

But the recovery struggled to hold, with the latest completed five-minute bar at the supplied 4:50 p.m. cutoff closing near $76.83.

That leaves Intel approximately 16.6% below its pre-earnings reference.

The important distinction now is between a temporary rebound following aggressive selling and a more convincing recovery in which buyers begin to regain control.

Intel share-price levels to watch

$77.15-$80.00: The first recovery decision area

This is the immediate region traders should monitor.

A sustained reclaim would suggest that buyers are becoming more successful in absorbing the initial selling pressure.

Repeated failures beneath the area, particularly if accompanied by lower rebound highs, would favor continued caution.

$84.60-$86.20: The more significant recovery test

Reaching this region would represent meaningful progress beyond the first rebound.

It is also important because it includes the lower boundary of the supplied pre-event options-implied price range.

An implied range reflects options pricing expectations, not a guaranteed limit on how far a stock can move.

$71.20-$72.55: The initial selloff-low region

A return toward this area could become particularly informative.

If selling slows and buyers establish a higher low, the market may be starting to absorb the earnings disappointment.

A sustained breakdown would weaken that interpretation.

$69.70-$70.00: The next lower observation area

If the initial low fails decisively, this becomes the next downside area to monitor.

It is not a prediction that Intel must reach $70.

Why the Nasdaq reaction matters too

One of the most useful observations is that Amazon and Intel weakened considerably more than the technology benchmark during the initial reaction.

Nasdaq futures declined approximately 1.23% over the comparable observation window.

Amazon underperformed that move by about 5.16 percentage points, while Intel underperformed by roughly 15.33 percentage points.

This matters because it helps distinguish a broad market decline from selling pressure concentrated in individual companies.

The relative weakness suggests that stock-specific earnings information was an important part of the market's repricing. It does not establish the precise contribution of every headline or the direction of causation.

There is also a broader context to this earnings week.

In investingLive's earlier Amazon and Intel earnings preview, the central question was whether AI-driven growth could justify the spending and support future cash flow.

That question now looks particularly relevant.

The selling also follows Alphabet's sharp earnings reaction, where strong cloud growth was overshadowed by concerns surrounding search performance and heavy investment.

However, it would be premature to conclude that investors have turned against AI investment universally.

Different companies have different cash-generation profiles, demand trends and expectations already reflected in their valuations.

What these results suggest is that the market is becoming more demanding about the financial returns on AI investment, not necessarily questioning whether demand for AI infrastructure exists.

Friday, October 30: What would change the picture?

The next regular trading session could provide a more useful test of how durable the initial repricing becomes.

A constructive recovery

Amazon reclaims its first recovery zone and makes progress toward $232.30-$234.90, while Intel can hold above $77.15-$80.00 and build higher lows.

Such behavior would suggest that at least part of the initial selling pressure is being absorbed.

Continued selling pressure

Amazon fails to defend the $224.90-$229.10 region and moves toward $219.70, while Intel repeatedly fails below $80 and returns toward $71.20-$72.55.

That would suggest the early rebounds were insufficient to establish meaningful stabilization.

No clear resolution

Both stocks move erratically within their large after-hours ranges, with neither buyers nor sellers gaining convincing control.

In that case, waiting for better price confirmation may be more useful than trying to predict the next move from an isolated price spike.

The first 30-60 minutes of Friday's regular session deserve attention, particularly in relation to Nasdaq futures and the price zones above. However, the opening period can also produce false breaks and substantial volatility.

The scheduled company conference calls may materially change expectations before that session begins.

The lesson from Amazon and Intel earnings

There is a useful distinction here for traders and investors.

Amazon has demonstrated rapid cloud growth and record operating profitability, but its heavy spending is putting pressure on free cash flow.

Intel has demonstrated substantial improvement in data-center demand and margins, but the next-quarter outlook is considerably weaker than investors expected.

Both developments can be true at the same time.

For longer-term investors, the important questions concern sustainable growth, capital efficiency, execution and valuation.

For shorter-term traders, the next opportunity to learn something comes from how prices behave after the initial earnings shock.

Strong results can still disappoint a market with even stronger expectations. And sometimes, the reaction to the reaction tells us more than the first move itself.

item.title: BoJ preview: hold at 1.25% expected, with 2% inflation call and dissent risk in focus
item.description:
The yen and short-end Japanese government bond yields are where the reaction will show. A clear 2% declaration, a firm Ueda and a hawkish dissent would likely support the yen, push two-year yields higher and add to December pricing. Dovish dissents calling for a cut could outweigh hawkish language and trigger renewed yen selling, a risk sharpened by the yen’s heavy losses earlier this year. Oil remains a key swing factor: further gains in crude, tied to the conflict in the Middle East, strengthen the case for faster tightening because energy feeds directly into Japan’s import costs and inflation outlook. USD/JPY is also still digesting this week’s Federal Reserve meeting.

---

Earlier:

  • BOJ preview: Daiwa sees hold, but 2% inflation call could open door to December hike
  • BoJ preview: MUFG sees hold but a 2% inflation call, with two dissenters the key yen risk
  • BOJ to hold at 1.25%, but Ueda signals further hikes toward neutral
  • BOJ seen lifting rates to 1.50% in December as 69% of economists expect a Q4 hike
  • BOJ reportedly may upgrade inflation forecast, hold rates steady at next week's meeting

---

The Bank of Japan looks set to stand still this week, but a formal nod to 2% inflation and a split board could do the moving for it.

Summary:

  • The BoJ is widely expected to hold its policy rate at 1.25%; a hike this week is seen as very unlikely
  • Analysts expect the Outlook Report to effectively declare that underlying inflation has reached 2%, with inflation and growth forecasts nudged higher on oil
  • Markets price roughly a 73% chance of a December hike; 69% of economists in a Reuters poll expect 1.50% this quarter
  • Dissent risk runs both ways: two members who opposed September’s hike could call for a cut, while Takata may push for a hike
  • Ueda’s press conference language, especially any move toward “next meeting” phrasing, is a key December signal
  • Easing inflation expectations argue for patience, while oil, cost pass-through and yen weakness argue for further tightening

The Bank of Japan is widely expected to keep its policy rate at 1.25% when it concludes its two-day meeting on Friday. Markets are focused less on the decision than on whether the board signals a hike in December.

A move this week would be a major surprise. The central bank raised rates in June and again in September, taking its benchmark to the highest level in 31 years, and traders were pricing virtually no chance of back-to-back tightening heading into the meeting. A Nikkei report citing a senior official said consecutive hikes would only be considered in a serious emergency. Market pricing pointed to roughly a 73% chance of a further increase in December. A Reuters poll of 78 economists found 69% expect the rate to reach 1.50% this quarter, with most of those naming December.

The main event is likely to be the quarterly Outlook Report. Analysts broadly expect the board to effectively declare that underlying inflation has reached its 2% price stability target. That shift would move policy from lifting inflation toward keeping it stable. Governor Kazuo Ueda said earlier this month that, with underlying inflation close to 2%, the bank could not tolerate a further rise. A Reuters report citing sources familiar with the central bank’s thinking said policymakers may also nudge up their fiscal 2027 inflation forecast as higher oil prices feed through to consumer prices. Analysts at one Japanese brokerage expect upgrades to the growth and core inflation projections, driven mainly by crude.

The vote could be as important as the statement. Two board members opposed the September hike, and MUFG flagged the risk that they dissent against a hold and call for a cut. That would reinforce a dovish image and could trigger yen selling. Other analysts expect board member Hajime Takata to dissent in the opposite direction, proposing a hike as he did in July.

Ueda’s press conference will be watched for any change in language. If he moves away from saying rates are decided at every meeting toward phrasing that points to the next meeting, markets would likely read it as a strong December signal. A more guarded tone, focused on reviewing financial conditions after the September increase, could trim hike expectations.

There are reasons for caution. October surveys showed household and business inflation expectations easing, and sources told Reuters there is little evidence of a broader wage-price spiral. ING expects a hold now, followed by two hikes in 2027. Against that, several forces keep pressure on the central bank to continue tightening: oil-driven price pressure linked to the conflict in the Middle East, broadening cost pass-through to consumers and the risk of renewed yen weakness.

With the policy rate already inside the bank’s estimated neutral range of about 1% to 2.5%, the debate is shifting from whether the BoJ hikes again to how far it goes. Economists in the Reuters poll increasingly see a terminal rate of 2% or higher. 

Bank of Japan Governor Ueda news conference due at 0630 GMT. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: USDCHF tests key support as sellers challenge the 200-hour moving average
item.description:
The USDCHF is trading near session lows after breaking below its 100-hour moving average at 0.82758. That break gave sellers the technical go-ahead to push lower, with the decline extending to 0.8257, right at the 200-hour moving average. The price has since edged back to around 0.8262, leaving traders with a clearly defined battle between buyers and sellers.

The distinction between those two moving averages is important. The break below the 100-hour moving average shifted the near-term bias toward the sellers. However, reaching the 200-hour moving average introduces another decision point. Sellers have reached a downside target. To strengthen their control, they now need to break below that target and stay below it.

For buyers, the same level offers an opportunity to define and limit risk.

The buyer’s perspective: Define risk before entry

Why would a buyer step in when the price is falling? Because a technical trade does not require certainty that the market has bottomed. It requires a reason to enter, a clear point at which the trade idea is wrong, and enough potential reward to justify the risk.

A buyer leaning against the 200-hour moving average near 0.8257 is looking for that level to attract support. If the price holds above it and begins to recover, the buyer benefits from entering close to support. If the price breaks below and selling gathers momentum, the reason for the trade weakens, giving the buyer a nearby reference point for exiting.

That is an important trading lesson: the moving average does not guarantee a bounce. It provides a level around which a trader can build a plan. Risk can be defined before entry, limited through an exit strategy, and accepted as part of the trade.

The seller’s perspective: Turn an opinion into a technical plan

The bearish trader can use that same moving average from the opposite perspective.

If you expect the USDCHF to continue lower, the 200-hour moving average becomes a level the price needs to get to, get through, and stay below. A bearish opinion alone does not confirm that sellers are in control. The price action around support provides evidence of whether other traders agree.

A sustained break below 0.8257, followed by an inability to reclaim the moving average, would suggest buyers are losing that battle. If a subsequent rebound stalls against the moving average from below, former support could become resistance. That would give sellers another reference point for managing risk.

Conversely, a brief dip below the moving average followed by a quick recovery would raise the possibility of a failed break. Sellers looking for downside follow-through could become vulnerable if the market cannot remain below support.

Downside targets: What comes after a break?

On a sustained break lower, the next downside target comes at the 38.2% retracement at 0.8224. That level sits near the upper boundary of a swing area extending down to 0.82162.

Together, those levels form another support zone where traders would assess whether the selling can continue. Reaching the zone would satisfy another downside objective. Breaking through it—and staying below—would strengthen the bearish case further.

A break below that zone would open the door toward last week’s low at 0.81905.

The recovery scenario: What buyers need to reclaim

If the 200-hour moving average holds, buyers would first look for a recovery toward the 100-hour moving average at 0.82758.

Holding support would be an initial positive, but reclaiming that higher moving average would provide stronger evidence that buyers are regaining control. The move would also call into question the earlier downside break, increasing the potential for sellers to cover positions.

Staying above the 100-hour moving average would put yesterday’s high at 0.8312 back in focus.

The key lesson: Let the price action guide the trade

For now, 0.8257 is the key barometer. Buyers can use it to define risk on a support trade. Sellers need a sustained break below it to reinforce the bearish bias.

The value of the technical level is that it gives both sides a reference point. Traders can measure whether the market is supporting their position and identify when the evidence changes.

Have an opinion, but build the trade around a level that defines your risk. Then let the price action determine whether the trade deserves to stay open.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

3. Lift the US naval blockade. End restrictions on Iranian ports, tankers and commercial shipping.

4. Remove economic and political sanctions. Restore Iran's ability to export oil and conduct international financial transactions.

5. Withdraw US naval and air forces from the region. End the American military deployments and operations that Tehran regards as threatening Iran.

7. End threats and hostile interference. Stop military threats, hostile rhetoric and what Tehran considers interference in its internal affairs.

item.title: Boeing stock analysis: Is the earnings selloff a buy-the-dip opportunity?
item.description:
Boeing stock rebounds after a 10.7% earnings plunge. Is the next dip worth buying?

Boeing shares are recovering from a sharp selloff, but the next pullback could tell investors more than the rebound itself. Here's why the $169-$171 area matters, what could support a longer-term recovery and how a hypothetical position might manage the risk.

Boeing (NYSE: BA) is showing signs of recovery after a painful post-earnings selloff. But is this the beginning of a longer-term buying opportunity or just a temporary rebound? I'm particularly interested in whether buyers can defend the $169-$171 area on the next pullback, rather than simply chasing the stock higher.

As of approximately 11:50 a.m. New York time on October 29, Boeing shares were trading around $173.60, up approximately 3.9% from Wednesday's close, based on delayed intraday data.

That's an encouraging recovery, but it follows a substantial decline.

Boeing shares plunged 10.7% on October 27, closing at $168.18 after trading at $188.31 immediately before earnings. The selling continued on October 28, when shares reached $165.01 before closing at $167.14.

The question now is whether the market has sufficiently adjusted to the earnings disappointment, or whether sellers will return when the initial enthusiasm fades.

Boeing's earnings weren't all bad. So why did the stock plunge?

Boeing's third-quarter earnings report contained several positive developments.

Revenue reached $24.2 billion, up 4% year over year. The company generated approximately $464 million in quarterly free cash flow, reported a record $745 billion backlog and continued to make progress on important aircraft certification programs.

The FAA's recent certification of Boeing's 737 MAX 10 was another meaningful milestone, opening the way for deliveries of an aircraft with substantial existing orders.

But there is a difference between having strong demand and converting that demand into profitable aircraft deliveries.

That distinction helps explain the negative market reaction.

As Reuters reported, Boeing's progress toward producing 47 737 aircraft per month has been slower than anticipated, with that production milestone now expected in early 2027.

The company also outlined approximately $3 billion in expected free cash flow for 2027, below the $5.5 billion analyst consensus cited by Reuters. Its $10 billion annual free-cash-flow ambition has shifted to 2029.

There's another important number investors should monitor.

Despite generating positive free cash flow in the third quarter, Boeing's cumulative free cash flow for the first nine months of 2026 remained negative at approximately $359 million.

To achieve its roughly $2 billion full-year free-cash-flow expectation, Boeing would therefore need to generate approximately $2.36 billion in the fourth quarter.

That's a substantial amount of cash generation still to deliver.

The company's backlog provides potential future revenue, but execution, production efficiency and cash conversion will determine how much value eventually reaches shareholders.

The next Boeing stock pullback could be more revealing than today's rally

For a possible longer-term buy-the-dip opportunity, I would focus on a few specific price areas.

$169-$171: The first area I want buyers to defend

This is perhaps the most interesting near-term support candidate.

Boeing struggled to sustain a recovery above this region immediately following its earnings selloff. Thursday's rally has now carried shares beyond it.

What happens if the stock returns?

If Boeing pulls back toward $169-$171, briefly slips below part of that area but recovers, and then establishes a higher low, I would view that as potentially constructive.

It would suggest buyers are becoming more willing to defend prices that previously presented difficulties.

The important point is not merely touching $170. It is how the stock behaves around that price and whether buying interest persists after the initial rebound.

A successful defense during broader stock-market weakness would be particularly interesting, although not conclusive.

$165-$167: A deeper test of whether a bottom is developing

Wednesday's low of $165.01 provides a useful reference.

If Boeing revisits this area, buyers would have another opportunity to demonstrate that selling pressure is weakening.

Even a temporary move below $165 followed by a convincing recovery could still be consistent with a developing bottom.

However, sustained trading beneath the area, particularly if attempted recoveries repeatedly fail, would weaken the bullish interpretation.

$174-$176 and $178-$179: Recovery checkpoints

On the upside, $174-$176 represents the first nearby area to monitor.

Beyond that, $178-$179 is a more meaningful recovery checkpoint.

A move above these areas, followed by an ability to hold them during subsequent pullbacks, would strengthen the case that the recovery is becoming more durable.

A sustained improvement could eventually bring the $188-$190 region back into view, near Boeing's pre-earnings trading prices.

None of these outcomes is guaranteed. They are observable tests that can help investors assess whether a rebound is developing into something more substantial.

An educational Boeing buy-the-dip strategy for longer-term investors

One lesson I find useful when considering a stock following a sharp decline is that a good-looking price and a good entry are not necessarily the same thing.

An investor might like Boeing at $169.50, but a return to that price alone would not establish that the stock is ready to recover.

For illustration, consider a hypothetical strategy that waits for a pullback into the $168-$171 region, followed by evidence of stabilization and renewed buying.

The following example assumes an entry at $169.50. It is not a recommendation to buy at that price, and no future entry or execution is assumed.

Conditional entry: $169.50

Only after a qualifying pullback and signs that buyers are defending the area. The price may never return there, or the necessary confirmation may develop at a different price.

Protective stop: $157.50

This places the initial exit level beneath the recent $165.01 low and the deeper $160 reference area. It provides more room for volatility than a tight short-term stop but exposes the investor to a larger potential loss.

Initial risk: $12 per share, approximately 7.1%

The risk calculation assumes execution at the stated entry and stop, before costs, slippage or price gaps.

First profit target: $188

Potential reward of $18.50 per share, or approximately 1.54 times the initial risk.

Second profit target: $210

Potential reward of $40.50 per share, or approximately 3.38 times the initial risk.

Third profit target: $235

Potential reward of $65.50 per share, or approximately 5.46 times the initial risk.

Intended holding period: 6-12 months

The targets are illustrative recovery milestones, not forecasts or estimates of the probability that Boeing will reach them.

An investor could consider selling one-third of the original position at each target.

Another optional approach would be to move the protective stop on the remaining shares to the original entry price after the first profit target is reached.

That could reduce the remaining position's exposure to an ordinary price reversal, although a subsequent pullback could also stop out the remaining shares before a larger recovery.

Importantly, a stop at the entry price does not guarantee a breakeven exit. Gaps, slippage and trading costs can affect actual results.

And the 1.54, 3.38 and 5.46 reward-to-risk figures describe individual targets relative to the original risk, not the expected profitability of the overall strategy.

What could go wrong with a Boeing buy-the-dip investment?

There are two separate risks to consider.

The first is price action.

A strong rebound immediately after a large decline can sometimes attract buyers without representing a sustainable change in direction.

If Boeing cannot maintain the $169-$171 area, falls below $165 and repeatedly fails to recover, the argument for an emerging bottom would deteriorate.

The second risk is fundamental.

Boeing is still working through a complicated operational recovery. Production targets, supply-chain constraints, aircraft deliveries, manufacturing quality and free-cash-flow generation remain important uncertainties.

Even if the company makes genuine progress, its shares could struggle if actual results fall short of expectations.

And a stock recovering technically does not automatically mean its valuation is attractive for a six-to-twelve-month investment.

Investors should also weigh Boeing's debt, prospective earnings and cash flow against the price they are being asked to pay.

An alternative is simply to wait.

An investor seeking greater confirmation could allow Boeing to reclaim $178-$179, or even demonstrate a more sustained recovery toward its pre-earnings prices.

That might mean paying more for the shares, but potentially with stronger evidence that the immediate selling pressure has diminished.

Waiting for confirmation has its own trade-offs, but there is no requirement to participate in every potential bottom.

My bottom line on Boeing stock

I find Boeing interesting after its substantial earnings-related decline, particularly because the company's long-term demand picture has not disappeared.

But the market has also received genuine reasons to question the speed and profitability of its turnaround.

For now, the $169-$171 area is the first price region I would watch carefully.

If buyers defend it, establish a higher low and eventually overcome the next recovery checkpoints, the case for a longer-term position could improve.

If those defenses fail, there may be a better opportunity later, or no opportunity worth taking under the current assumptions.

The objective isn't to predict Boeing's exact bottom. It's to identify what the stock needs to demonstrate before putting capital at risk.

Educational only. Trade at your own risk. The hypothetical strategy is not personalized investment advice. Prices, levels and conditions should be reassessed against current market data before any investment decision.

This article was written by Itai Levitan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Gold slips below its 100-hour MA as interest-rate concerns weigh on the recovery
item.description:
Fundamentally, and the recent him broader view, gold’s retreat from its August high reflects a market more concerned about higher interest rates than attracted to its protection against inflation and geopolitical uncertainty. Higher Treasury yields, a firm dollar and expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening have made it difficult for buyers to sustain a recovery.

That highlights an important distinction for gold traders. Although gold is often viewed as an inflation hedge, higher inflation does not automatically translate into higher gold prices. If inflation leads investors to expect tighter monetary policy and higher yields, the interest-rate response can outweigh demand for inflation protection. Gold pays no interest, so higher yields increase the opportunity cost of holding the metal. A stronger dollar can add another headwind by making dollar-denominated gold more expensive for buyers using other currencies.

Spot gold fell to $3,975 last Friday, its lowest level since mid-July, before recovering above the psychologically important $4,000 level early this week. Lower oil prices helped ease inflation concerns, offering some relief from the pressure surrounding the interest-rate outlook. However, that rebound has struggled to develop into a more convincing recovery.

The Fed’s decision to hold rates unchanged yesterday did little to remove that headwind. Attention has already shifted toward December, with the market pricing in approximately an 84% probability of a rate increase, according to the pricing cited. A pause in October therefore does not necessarily signal an end to the tightening cycle. As long as another hike remains heavily priced, gold buyers face a difficult backdrop.

That does not prevent corrective rallies. It does, however, put greater importance on whether those rallies can clear technical resistance and hold above it.

Wednesday’s recovery stalled at a key technical barometer

Technically, buyers pushed gold toward $4,080 on Wednesday, but the advance stalled near the falling 200-hour moving average. Sellers leaned against that resistance and pushed the price back to the downside.

The location of that reversal matters. A recovery toward a widely watched moving average gives buyers an opportunity to demonstrate greater control. When the price fails to break above that level, sellers have a defined area against which to limit risk. Wednesday’s rejection left the recovery incomplete and reinforced the importance of the 200-hour moving average as an overhead barometer.

Until buyers can move above—and stay above—that moving average, sellers retain an important technical advantage.

The 100-hour MA is the immediate battleground

In trading today, gold has extended below its 100-hour moving average at $4,026.50 (blue line on the chart above). The price is trading near $4,025, down approximately $41, or 1.03%, leaving it just below that technical level.

Lower Treasury yields today have offered some support and helped slow the decline. Nevertheless, buyers still need to turn that support into a sustained move back above the 100-hour moving average.

For traders, the distinction is between a brief break and acceptance below the level. A quick recovery above $4,026.50 would suggest the downside break is failing, giving buyers an initial foothold. Holding above it would then bring attention back toward Wednesday’s high near $4,080 and the falling 200-hour moving average.

Conversely, if rebounds stall at or below the 100-hour moving average, the former support would begin acting as resistance. That would keep sellers in control of the immediate bias.

A sustained break lower would expose the October low

On the downside, $4,000 is the next psychological reference point, followed by the October low at $3,975.40. A break below that low would extend the decline and expose the broader swing area between $3,942.71 and $3,959.37, defined by lows going back to June and July.

That swing area would become an important test of whether buyers are willing to defend longer-standing support. Buyers leaning against it would have a defined risk level below the zone. A sustained break beneath it would weaken the broader technical picture further.

For now, $4,026.50 is the close-risk barometer. Below it, sellers retain the immediate advantage, with $4,000 and $3,975.40 in focus. Above it, buyers can begin repairing today’s technical damage—but clearing the falling 200-hour moving average remains the more significant hurdle.

Gold technical ladder: the levels defining the next move

The 100-hour moving average at $4,026.50 is the immediate barometer for buyers and sellers. Holding below it keeps the near-term bias tilted lower, while a sustained recovery above would give buyers an initial foothold.

On the topside, the next key hurdle is the $4,080 area, where Wednesday’s rally stalled near the falling 200-hour moving average. Buyers need to clear that resistance to strengthen the recovery.

Below the market, $4,000 provides a psychological reference point ahead of the October low at $3,975.40. A break below that low would expose the broader $3,942.71–$3,959.37 swing area, defined by lows from June and July.

The ladder provides a framework for managing risk: watch whether price breaks a level and holds beyond it, or fails and reverses. A failed break can be just as revealing as a sustained breakout, particularly when buyers and sellers are battling around a widely followed moving average.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: The door remains ajar for ECB to tighten. EURUSD rebounds after break lower failed
item.description:
The ECB kept interest rates unchanged as expected, but President Christine Lagarde delivered a hawkish message despite the decision to hold. Policymakers discussed a rate increase, and Lagarde indicated that conditions could have justified additional tightening. The decision to wait reflected unchanged underlying inflation and uncertainty surrounding the outlook, rather than a declaration that the tightening cycle was over.

For EURUSD, the decision and press conference produced volatile trading. An initial decline took the price below the double bottom near 1.11135, established on October 14 and revisited yesterday. However, sellers could not sustain the break. After reaching 1.1106, the pair reversed higher and rebounded toward 1.1155.

That recovery brought the price into a familiar swing area, with the falling 100-hour moving average just above. The failed break lower gives buyers an opportunity, but getting through resistance is the next requirement.

A hawkish hold keeps the next meeting in focus

Lagarde stressed that holding rates at this meeting does not rule out an increase at the next. Underlying inflation remains a key policy barometer, while elevated energy prices and geopolitical developments continue to complicate the outlook.

The distinction matters. A central bank can leave rates unchanged while still delivering a hawkish message if its guidance keeps further tightening in play. Markets respond to changes in the expected path of rates, as well as the decision announced that day.

Underlying inflation helps policymakers assess how persistent price pressures are beneath volatile headline components. Higher energy costs can lift headline inflation directly, but the broader concern is whether those increases feed into other prices, wages and inflation expectations.

The ECB’s message leaves room to gather more evidence while retaining the option to act.

Incoming data will shape the next decision

On growth, the ECB will assess incoming GDP figures alongside wages, unemployment and November PMIs to judge how the economy is absorbing tighter financing conditions. Updated staff projections and two additional inflation reports will also help shape the next decision.

Those releases matter because monetary policy works with a lag. Higher borrowing costs gradually influence household spending, business investment and demand. Policymakers must judge whether that restraint is sufficient to bring inflation down, or whether persistent price pressures require another increase.

For traders, this keeps the focus on how the data change expectations. Persistent inflation alongside resilient activity could strengthen the case for further tightening. Softer inflation and weaker growth could support another period of waiting.

The break below 1.11135 fails to attract follow-through

Technically, the initial move below 1.11135 gave sellers an opportunity to extend the decline (see chart above). That level had attracted buyers twice, making it an identifiable floor and a logical downside barometer.

However, the move to 1.1106 quickly reversed.

A support break needs follow-through to reinforce the bearish signal. When the price moves below a well-defined floor and then quickly recovers above it, the failure can encourage short covering and fresh buying. Traders who sold the break may find themselves holding positions below a reclaimed support level.

That does not automatically establish a lasting bottom. It does show that sellers failed to maintain control below the old floor. Buyers now need to build on that rejection by breaking resistance above.

Buyers face resistance at 1.1152–1.11616

The rebound toward 1.1155 carried EURUSD into the swing area between 1.1152 and 1.11602. Just above that zone sits the falling 100-hour moving average at 1.11616.

Together, those levels create the first important resistance hurdle.

Swing areas identify prices where the market has previously changed direction or found support and resistance. Moving averages provide another reference for judging momentum and defining risk. When those references sit close together, they create a useful decision zone for buyers and sellers.

A move above—and sustained trading above—1.11616 would strengthen the buyers’ position. A brief spike through resistance followed by a reversal would carry less weight.

Above that hurdle, the next upside targets are:

  • 1.11845: The former floor from October 15 through October 26.

  • 1.11913: The falling 200-hour moving average.

The old floor matters because broken support can become resistance when approached from below. Clearing it, followed by the 200-hour moving average, would provide further evidence that buyers are gaining control.

The technical ladder highlights the levels that will help determine whether the EURUSD rebound can extend or sellers regain control.

Resistance, from highest to lowest:

  • 1.11913 — Falling 200-hour moving average: A higher hurdle that buyers would need to clear to strengthen the bullish bias.

  • 1.11845 — Former floor from October 15–26: Previously support, this level becomes potential resistance when approached from below.

  • 1.11616 — Falling 100-hour moving average: A key barometer for the recovery. Getting above and staying above would give buyers a stronger foothold.

  • 1.1152–1.11602 — Swing resistance area: The rebound high near 1.1155 reached inside this zone, making it the immediate battleground.

Support, from highest to lowest:

  • 1.11130–1.11135 — Reclaimed support near the prior double bottom: Holding above this area would help preserve the failed-break recovery. Falling back below would weaken that argument.

  • 1.1106 — Session low: Sellers would need a sustained break below this level to confirm a fresh downside extension.

Trading lesson: These levels provide places to assess the price action and define risk. Sellers leaning against resistance have a clear reference for when their bearish view starts to weaken. Buyers looking for a breakout need sustained trading above resistance, followed ideally by that area holding as support on a retest.

For now, 1.1152–1.11616 is the immediate decision zone. Clearing it opens the door toward 1.11845 and 1.11913. A rejection keeps the reclaimed floor near 1.11135 in focus.
